Guptas: Road to Exit

By: Anna-Maria van Niekerk | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How did we get to this point where the Gupta family and finance Minister wage open battles in the media and court -- affecting the President's immediate future?

Unique Selling Point:
Drawing on Carte Blanche's stories of the last two years, we present an overview of the actions and reactions from major roleplayers that have led the President, the ruling party, the economy and the public to the edge of breakdown.

Summary:
We will draw together the content and meaning of events that we followed in detail at the time -- Guptagate, Nenegate, Nkandlagate, 2016 municipal elections and the dramatic Public Protector investigation on state capture. This story will provide not only a bird's eye view of the big picture, we will recap the insights and analysis that we assembled in the months that the country was dragged through daily dramatic headlines.

Press Release:


Guptas: Road to Exit
South Africa is in a precarious position. No-one would have predicted that a post-apartheid, sitting president’s reputation would be so shattered through links to the powerful Gupta family and their clique, that the top brass in his own political party would begin to rise up against him. Is South Africa facing a tipping point? Carte Blanche brings key insight through exposés and investigations conducted over the years.

PROMOS TEN:
A post-apartheid president’s reputation has been so shattered through links to one powerful family that his colleagues begin to oppose him. Are we at a tipping point?


FIFTEEN:
8 secs On tenterhooks, South Africans wait to see what will happen to our finance minister, president Zuma, and the well-connected family that allegedly started all the trouble…
MCEBISI: The Presidency has literally been captured.

FIFTEEN:
AUBREY MATSHIQI: There has been little evidence that president and other in ANC regard national interest of primary concern...
10 secs We review years of damning revelations on the President and the family who befriended the country’s powerful.



Script:


GUPTAS: ROAD TO EXIT
PRODUCERS: ESTE DE KLERK & ANNA-MARIA VAN NIEKERK
EDITOR: STENETTE GROSSKOPF
TX: 23 OCTOBER 2016

BONGANI LINK: Beyond all expectations South Africa’s transition to democracy was something of a miracle – from near calamity we became lauded for one of the most progressive constitutions in the world with strong institutions to safeguard our freedoms. Yet we find ourselves back at the edge of the precipice as the very foundations of what we have built are being threatened – how did we get here?
It started with an “alleged” questionable relationship between one family and the president.
SOLLY MAPAILA: They seen as untouchables.
FERIAL HAFFAJEE: Wherever the state had a big hand you would see they would go and open up a new entry point there.
PRINCE MASHELE: These people still have big plans to further capture the state.
2013 VO: The Gupta family has been called South Africa’s “shadow government” ...accused of wielding enormous political influence in South Africa, with critics saying they’re “capturing the state” to advance their own business interests.
APRIL 2016 DEVI LINK: They are known for their power, influence and money. But who exactly are the Guptas? A family who have, in just 23 years, rose up from selling shoes from the boot of their car to having to significant influence on the most powerful man in our country.
GUPTAGATE – 2013
In 2013, the friendship secured them permission to land their plane at Waterkloof Airforce Base to ferry guests to Sun City for a family wedding.
MAY 2013 BARRY BATEMAN: Cars that were lined up to leave the air force base – at the front of them there was the police flying squad.
A internal inquiry fingered two commanding officers...they in turn fingered Number One.
VO: The report quoted Chief of State Protocol Bruce Koloane saying he was “under pressure from No.1” while Lt Col Anderson said: “our Number 1 knows about this.”
MAY 2013 Carte Blanche revealed that the Guptas came into the radar of national intelligence by 2011, but official orders prevented an investigation. Service head Mo Shaik resigned. All he would say was this:
MO SHAIK: “The law, the binding oath taken and the ethics of the profession, all forbid me from discussing any aspect of work that I dealt with during my time as the head of the South African Secret Service. Accordingly, under these obligations and irrespective of any offence I take as a South African on this narcissistic breach of our national security, I decline the offer to comment on the record.”
Critics felt the president waited far too long to explain himself.
MAY 2013 PRINCE MASHELE: He should have addressed the nation and said: South Africans, I know that you are very concerned about what has happened. I have a relationship with the Gupta family, I think the family has taken advantage of my relationship with them, I have taken the decision to cut them off. I want us to start afresh, please trust me.
NENEGATE – DECEMBER 2015
Not only did Number One not take the nation into his confidence in 2013, he stunned the nation two years later by sacking his respected Finance Minister.
DEC 2015 PRES ZUMA: I’ve decided to remove Mr Nhlanhla Nene as minister of finance.
Treasury had always been seen as too important to be meddled with -- the president put it in the hands of ANC backbencher Des van Rooyen.
DEC 2015 BEN TUROK: I was shocked and frankly upset know him well. He is a decent man of integrity.
The fierce outcry from civil society and the financial world saw Van Rooyen lasting only four days before former finance minister Pravin Gordhan -- then Minister of Cooperative Governance, was reinstated.
IRAJ ABEDIAN: Minister Gordhan came to rescue; to reestablish communication for the Cabinet, to give the South African government enough credibility in the global financial market to be able to borrow.
BONGANI LINK: Miraculously, the president survived the blunder -- even though it later emerged the ANC top brass had neither been consulted, nor informed about the Nene move. The cracks were beginning to show.
In February, five days before Minister Gordhan was due to deliver the annual Budget Speech, he was told the Hawks were investigating him for the so-called SARS Rogue Unit, established in 2007 to probe tax defaulters, when he’d been SARS Commissioner. The Hawks would also investigate his approval for an administrative matter after he became Minister.
In March the largest banks dumped the Guptas as clients; AND Deputy Finance Minister Mcebisi Jonas broke ranks.
16 MARCH 2016 MCEBISI JONAS: Members of the Gupta family offered me the position of Minister of Finance to replace then Mr Nene. I rejected this out of hand.
APRIL 2016 DEVI LINK: Mcebisi Jonas’s revelation that he was offered a position as Minister was the first high-ranking Minister confirming the Guptas’ ties to the President.
BONGANI LINK: Opposition parties, organised labour and struggle stalwarts called on the Public Protector to investigate allegations of state capture.

NKANDLAGATE – 2008-2016
BONGANI LINK: The Constitutional Court is the highest authority in the land and it has found president Zuma wanting…
The Constitutional Court found the President and Parliament had violated the Constitution in failing to implement Public Protector Advocate Thuli Madonsela's 2012 remedial action on the quarter-of-a-billion-rand upgrades at Nkandla.
31 MARCH 2016 JUSTICE MOGOENG MOGOENG: The President’s failure to comply with the remedial action taken against him by the Public Protector is inconsistent with his obligations to uphold, defend and respect the Constitution.
1 APRIL 2016 ZUMA: In hindsight, there are many matters that could have been handled differently, and which should never have been allowed to drag on this long, which we deeply regret.
Instead of heeding opposition calls to impeach him, the ANC defended the President.
OUT...OR NOT? – APRIL 2016
The Gupta family left for Dubai at the start of April. Atul and Ajay Gupta resigned all their directorships in their Oakbay Group, as did their business associate, the president’s son Duduzane -- director of 12 companies in the Gupta empire with shares valued at R95-million.
APRIL 2016 PRINCE MASHELE: They’re not totally out of South Africa -- all they are doing is a tactic to make us rest on our laurels and we must not do that.  
Questions linger around Oakbay Resources and Energy. Its main asset, a uranium deposit bought with a loan from the Industrial Development Corporation hasn’t started production, though the IDC says Oakbay is up to date with loan repayments. The family’s Optimum coal mine drew fire for allegedly getting preferential treatment from Eskom, to the detriment of other coal suppliers.
LOSING GROUND – AUGUST 2016
The 2016 Local Government Elections may yet prove to have been a watershed.
BONGANI LINK: Until then President Zuma had poured scorn on anyone who said his party was losing support saying the voters did not care enough about his scandals. The results showed he couldn’t have been more wrong!
TINYIKO MALULEKE: Jacob Zuma as a national issue has dominated these elections.
AUBREY MATSHIQI: Because ANC is dominant party the country does not have a functioning centre itself for which we as a society can process strategic responses to the crisis we face in economy and society.
LIVE BY THE SWORD – OCTOBER 2016
Last week -- in what seemed a bid to mute anti-Zuma sentiment -- the NPA summonsed Minister Gordhan to appear in court on two charges of fraud, come November second.
12 OCTOBER 2016 UPS PRAVIN: South Africans should really ask themselves who are the Hawks or these few people in the Hawks really serving?
MCEBISI NDLETYANA: The presidency has been captured. The executive authority does not rest with the presidency.
Markets reeled again.
IRAJ ABEDIAN: Will convene the country’s growth for the next 30 years…
Gordhan moved swiftly last Friday to file an explosive affidavit, asking the High Court for an order that he -- as Finance Minister -- could not be forced to intervene with banks to re-open Gupta accounts.
By Monday this week Oakbay CEO, Nazeem Howa resigned citing "health reasons".
BONGANI LINK: A week in our politics has become a long time. Next Wednesday, Minister Gordhan is due to deliver his much anticipated mid-term budget speech. That is the plan – for now.
Meanwhile wait for the release of Adv. Madonsela's State Capture report -- pending court action by the President.
Newly appointed Public Protector, Busisiwe Mkhwebane submitted her responding affidavit to the urgent interdict on Friday. She made it clear that the state capture report will be made public if the court orders this.
AUBREY: Over past few months there has been little evidence that president and other in ANC regard national interest of primary concern.
